question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt this hybrid root-plus-named-accounts configuration as its supported long-term multi-bot contract?
rationale: The feature introduces public config, setup, credential-routing, and persisted-state behavior; tests can verify mechanics, but only maintainers can approve the permanent product and upgrade contract.

options.title: Sponsor the account model
options.body: Remove the unrelated changes, complete exact-head compatibility review, and land the existing hybrid account design with legacy root configuration preserved.

options.title: Split the rollout
options.body: First land the account/config and monitor-routing foundation, then follow with Graph, setup, and persisted-state account scoping in separately reviewed PRs.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open but close or supersede this branch if maintainers do not want to own the expanded Teams configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the account model
recommendation.body: Remove the unrelated changes, complete exact-head compatibility review, and land the existing hybrid account design with legacy root configuration preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans public configuration, plugin architecture, upgrade policy, and a large Microsoft Teams channel change, and steipete is the documented project lead already subscribed to this PR.
